goal: Repair a source configuration and verify image, modules and early-userspace inputs.
context: Builds on supplied-source projects, module choices and boot-entry recovery. All source versions are fixed teaching fixtures, not a recommendation to deploy these kernels.

concepts.title: A kernel needs the drivers for its root disk
concepts.text: The kernel starts the system and manages hardware. This fixture has an NVMe disk containing an ext4 filesystem. It needs both the storage and filesystem drivers before it can reach the system root. Other hardware support is supplied by a fixed baseline.

concepts.title: Choose built-in, loadable or absent
concepts.text: In the five-setting fragment, y builds a driver into the image, m builds it as a separately loaded module, and n leaves it out. CONFIG_MODULES=y permits modules. CONFIG_BLK_DEV_INITRD=y lets this image load an external initramfs: a small early-userspace image that can load root drivers before the main system is available.

concepts.title: Save, build and inspect different outputs
concepts.text: Type configuration changes in the editor and select Save configuration. The build console reads that saved file. make bzImage builds image metadata; make modules builds module metadata; make all builds both when modules are enabled. CONFIG_LOCALVERSION adds a literal release suffix. Changing the editor or source leaves earlier outputs intact until rebuilt.

concepts.title: Early userspace must match its build
concepts.text: With m root drivers, build modules as well as the image, then use Assemble build initramfs. The model assembles the declared driver inputs for that exact source/configuration. With both root drivers built in, bare-device readiness can pass without an initramfs, but this assignment still requires external loading support. Readiness is not an actual boot or a UUID boot guarantee.

worked.explanation: Expected readiness: NVMe and ext4 support available. A successful make operation alone does not prove the resulting image has the needed drivers.

practice.title: Inspect and repair the example fragment
practice.action: In Configuration, change the missing NVMe setting from n to m. Select Save configuration.
practice.observe: The saved configuration summary changes. Earlier build outputs do not update when you edit the draft.

practice.title: Build the saved inputs
practice.action: Enter make all in the build console and select Run. Compare Image build and Module build with the selected source and release suffix.
practice.observe: Actual results list modeled outputs for the saved inputs. Change the release suffix, save it and build only bzImage to observe different image and module snapshots.

practice.title: Assemble, check and diagnose
practice.action: Rebuild with make all after any changed inputs. Select Assemble build initramfs, then Check build. Set NVMe back to n, save, rebuild and check again.
practice.observe: Actual objective feedback distinguishes missing drivers, unsaved changes and mismatched outputs. Retry with matching modular inputs or supported built-in choices.

requirements: Build the supplied target image with external initramfs-loading support and working NVMe/ext4 root-driver support.
Keep the saved configuration and build inputs consistent; a modular repair or supported built-in alternative may satisfy the task.

concepts.title: Stage beside the fallback
concepts.text: Builds still belong to the source workspace. Stage image places the versioned image inside the displayed virtual boot directory. make modules_install INSTALL_MOD_PATH=/training places matching module metadata under the example root. Assemble staged initramfs uses the selected staged image and module tree. These native controls are explicit simulator operations, not Linux commands to memorize.

concepts.title: Select the files the boot trial will actually use
concepts.text: A loader entry names a linux image and optional initrd path relative to virtual $BOOT. Its options identify the supplied root by UUID. In this exercise UUID lookup needs early userspace even if root drivers are built in. Save entry changes a virtual file; Check configuration then tests the candidate and checks that the original fallback files remain unchanged.

practice.title: Stage a candidate beside the fallback
practice.action: Select Stage image. Run make modules_install INSTALL_MOD_PATH=/training. Select the new staged image, then Assemble staged initramfs.
practice.observe: Virtual staged files show separate image, module and initramfs paths. An incorrect module root gives a missing-tree diagnostic; building modules is not the same as installing them.

practice.title: Save an independent boot selection
practice.action: Edit the candidate entry using the new staged paths and displayed root UUID. Select Save entry, then Check configuration. Keep fallback.conf unchanged.
practice.observe: Results distinguish the new target, boot handoff and preserved fallback. Try an incorrect root UUID and check again; restore it and retry.

requirements: Stage a working boot candidate from the supplied target source, using the saved configuration and a new loader-entry filename.
Preserve every original fallback image, module tree, initramfs and entry unchanged.
Verify a new-kernel boot through root and init handoff; booting the old fallback alone is insufficient.
